headline: High risk from shared filesystem and broad egress: CrewAI can feed Haystack untrusted content, leak data, and cascade errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and run browsers/subprocesses, while Haystack can consume MCP servers and REST APIs. That creates a plausible bridge where CrewAI-produced files or outputs are ingested by Haystack as instructions or prompts. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace that Haystack later reads
IF Haystack parses MCP or REST payloads as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Add provenance tags to all CrewAI outputs
Require Haystack to treat file content as untrusted data
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and Haystack has broad network egress plus MCP/REST access. If they share a workspace or credentials, CrewAI artifacts can be exposed to Haystack and then transmitted outward. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
IF CrewAI stores secrets or sensitive crew data in files that Haystack can read
IF Haystack forwards retrieved context to external APIs
mitigations: Use separate service accounts and credentials
Mount separate workspaces with no cross-read access
Redact secrets before writing CrewAI artifacts
Disable outbound calls for Haystack during shared-data runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and browser execution; Haystack can call REST/MCP endpoints and has broad egress. In a shared directory or shared mutable resource, both can modify the same artifacts without any locking shown in either profile. Because the default isolation is absent for CrewAI and coordination is undocumented, the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem path
IF Haystack writes back to artifacts that CrewAI also edits
IF no external lock or transaction layer is added
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator
Turn off concurrent runs on shared resources
Use file locks for any shared artifact
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework with shared memory, and Haystack is a search-RAG system that can consume upstream outputs. That makes it plausible that CrewAI-generated facts or citations become Haystack inputs and then drive downstream actions or responses without verification. The pairwise pathway is not directly evidenced, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF Haystack treats CrewAI output as authoritative context
IF CrewAI emits unverified facts that Haystack later retrieves or summarizes
IF downstream actions are triggered from Haystack outputs
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require source citations for all CrewAI claims
Have Haystack score confidence before acting
Log and review any cross-agent handoff
requires-engineering: add policy gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible. The other agent is cited because the risk is about cross-agent data handling, but the evidence is sparse.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into CrewAI crews
IF Haystack is configured to persist or export retrieved content beyond anonymous statistics
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review retention settings on both systems
Disable telemetry where possible
Document data-class boundaries for each agent
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
